question: Mission 6 of the NRRP provides for significant investments to strengthen placed-based assistance through Community Health and Welfare Centres, Community Hospitals and Territorial Operational Centres (Case della Comunità, Ospedali di Comunità and Centrali Operative Territoriali).

However, recent independent monitoring and official statistics from AGENAS1 have revealed some major problems: only 38 % of the Community Health and Welfare Centres seem to be operational, while fewer than than 3 % are actually operating with full teams of doctors and nurses. Delays are particularly acute in southern Italian regions.

There are also concerns over rising procurement costs, ongoing restructuring and de-funding, along with a persistent shortage of healthcare staff, making it difficult to guarantee that facilities which have already opened are fully operational.

Some regions dispute the AGENAS statistics2, but the disparities between the results of monitoring and region-byregion statements have raised doubts over transparency and the actual ability to reach the targets bound in with the NRRP payments. In the light of these problems, can the Commission state: 1.

Whether, on the basis of the information available, it considers there is a risk of the targets under Mission 6 – Health not being reached, particularly for the territorial network provided for in Ministerial Decree No 77/20223?
Whether it has carried out, or will carry out, additional checks on the actual state of play with the facilities that are being funded?
What measures could it take to help ensure that the NRRP investments yield fully operational and adequately staffed facilities?
Supporter4
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.5.2026) The written question refers to two targets related to Ministerial Decree N. 77/2022, specifically M6C1-3, concerning 1 038 health community houses, and M6C1-11, concerning 307 community hospitals1.

The Commission will assess the fulfilment of these two targets against the requirements enshrined in the Council Implementing Decision (CID) Annex2 in the context of the tenth payment request, which is expected to be submitted by Italy to the Commission later in 2026 (at the latest by 31 August 2026 in line with the Recovery and Resilience Facility Regulation3).

The Commission is in constant dialogue with the Italian Authorities on the implementation of the Italian recovery and resilience plan, with frequent technical meetings including on the abovementioned measures. The Commission understands that the statistics referred to in the written question reflect data from the first semester of 2025.

Furthermore, the Commission understands that the data at stake refer to the total number of structures planned including structures that are to be financed by national funds, hence outside the scope and timeframe of the Recovery and Resilience Facility.
The Commission will assess whether the relevant milestones and targets in the CID Annex have been satisfactorily fulfilled following the submission of a properly justified payment request by Italy.
1 The written question also refers to the Territorial Coordination Centres (Centrali Operative Territoriali), which

were already assessed in the context of the 7th payment request, in relation to target M6C1-7. 2 Annex to the Council Implementing Decision amending Implementing Decision (ST 10160/21 INIT; ST 10160/21 ADD 1 REV 2) of 13 July 2021 on the approval of the assessment of the recovery and resilience plan for Italy, https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15106-2025-ADD-1/en/pdf. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/european-union-recovery-and-resilience-facility.html.
